answer: Influence can depend on stake-weighted reputation earned through verified work. New identities start with little weight; established peers attest to useful outputs, which audits or downstream use can confirm. A whisper of fresh accounts cannot multiply one operator’s influence: each must build its own history. The attacker pays in locked capital, time, and real work, while colluding attestations risk slashing. Thus a plume of fake agents cannot cheaply harvest trust from the orchard.
